en-US.author: Fahrenheit Research
en-US.description: ArWen: GPU-native WRF-ARW-class regional weather model, verified against WRF v4.6.1
en-US.installationNotes:
This application requires an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support to run.
Will not function on integrated graphics or non-NVIDIA hardware.
Without compatible hardware, the application will fail to launch.
en-US.longDescription: ArWen is an independent, GPU-native implementation of a WRF-ARW-class regional atmospheric model. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by NCAR or UCAR. The name is a wordmark for "the ARW solver, GPU-native"; the Python package is currently named gpuwm. Safety. ArWen is a research and educational tool. It is never a substitute for official forecasts and warnings from your national meteorological service. Do not use it to make safety decisions. Regional numerical weather prediction at convective scale has mostly required institutional clusters, which means most of the world runs on global-model guidance at 10-25 km. ArWen's aim is to put a verified, kilometer-scale limited-area model on a single consumer GPU: pick a point, size a nest ladder to your card, pull public analysis data, and run a 1 km (or 500 m) simulation of your own area on hardware you own -- especially in places where no national convection-permitting model exists.
en-US.name: ArWen
en-US.releaseNotes:
New
- Opt-in ocean waves (`--waves on`) now also run on large lakes (5,000 km² or more). Depths come from ETOPO 2022, using the lake surface minus the lake bed. Lakes start calm, and their waves grow from forecast winds without an outside wave model. Checked in one case: a Lake Superior gale on 5 November 2026, with ArWen at 12 km for 9 hours and wave heights compared at three NDBC buoys. Lake ice is covered by a unit test only; lakes have not been validated against a season of buoy observations, and nests carry no waves.

Fixed
- `gpuwm go --waves on` now fetches the wave data bridge (`rw_waves_data`) from the release bundle on first use after a pip install. Previously it stopped with “rw_waves_data is required” unless `gpuwm fetch-bridges` had been run first.
- The wave bathymetry download now retries a range when the server ends it early. Previously, a single short range stopped the first `--waves on` run with “bathymetry acquisition incomplete”.
